identification.summary: Circle Typhoon is the Microsoft name for the China-based actor it first tracked as DEV-0322 [S8]. Microsoft attributed two campaigns to DEV-0322 with high confidence. The first, in July 2021, exploited a zero-day (CVE-2021-35211) in SolarWinds Serv-U [S1]. The second, from September 2021, exploited CVE-2021-40539 in Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus against defense-industrial-base, higher-education, consulting and IT organizations [S2]. Palo Alto Unit 42 tracks overlapping ManageEngine exploitation as the TiltedTemple campaign and links part of that activity to DEV-0322 [S3][S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft's first public DEV-0322 report is dated 2021-07-13 (Serv-U zero-day) [S1]. Microsoft first observed the ManageEngine campaign on 2021-09-22 [S2]. A SockDetour backdoor that Unit 42 associates with TiltedTemple infrastructure may have existed since July 2019, based on a compilation timestamp [S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft's naming mapping lists DEV-0322, EMISSARY PANDA (CrowdStrike), APT6 and APT27 (Mandiant) against Circle Typhoon [S8]. Microsoft also maps APT27 and Emissary Panda to Linen Typhoon (see the linen_extra record), so these vendor names are not exclusive to Circle Typhoon. Unit 42 did not formally attribute its ManageEngine campaign but noted similarities to earlier APT27 / Emissary Panda campaigns [S3][S4]. 'DEV-####' is Microsoft's temporary name for an emerging activity cluster [S2].

attribution.sponsor: China-based. Microsoft describes DEV-0322 as 'a group operating out of China' [S1][S2]. None of the sources gathered names a specific PRC state organization (MSS, MPS or PLA) as sponsor.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft MSTIC attributed both the Serv-U campaign [S1] and the ManageEngine campaign [S2] to DEV-0322 with high confidence. Unit 42 said only that its campaign resembled earlier APT27 / Emissary Panda activity [S3][S4]. Unit 42 could not say whether SockDetour activity came from one actor or several [S6]. No US government attribution of Circle Typhoon or DEV-0322 by name was found. CISA/FBI/CGCYBER AA21-259A attributes ManageEngine exploitation only to unnamed 'APT actors' [S7].
attribution.basis: For Serv-U, Microsoft cites victimology and tactics and procedures [S1]. For ManageEngine, Microsoft cites observed infrastructure, victimology, and tactics and procedures [S2]. Unit 42 relies on tooling and infrastructure correlation [S3][S5][S6].

objectives: Espionage access to defense-industrial-base and technology organizations. Microsoft reported targeting of US Defense Industrial Base entities and software companies [S1], plus higher education, consulting and IT [S2]. Unit 42 assessed the ManageEngine campaign as seeking persistent access and theft of sensitive documents (as reported in coverage) [S4]. Credential harvesting from domain controllers and authentication portals supports long-term access [S2][S3].

targeting.notes: Unit 42 reported at least 370 Zoho ManageEngine servers targeted in the United States alone, and at least nine organizations compromised worldwide between 2021-09-22 and early October 2021 [S3]. Later ServiceDesk Plus exploitation raised the TiltedTemple total to at least 13 compromised organizations [S5]. At least four US defense contractors were targeted with SockDetour, and at least one was compromised [S6]. Unit 42 sector and victim counts cover the TiltedTemple cluster and may not map one-to-one onto Microsoft's DEV-0322.

capabilities.summary: Exploits zero-day and newly disclosed vulnerabilities in internet-facing enterprise software: SolarWinds Serv-U SSH (CVE-2021-35211) [S1], ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus (CVE-2021-40539) [S2][S7], and ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus (CVE-2021-44077, linked by Unit 42) [S5]. Serv-U post-exploitation: spawning mshta, cmd and PowerShell; staging command output in the internet-reachable Serv-U Client\Common folder; creating a rogue Serv-U global administrator [S1]. ManageEngine post-exploitation: dumping credentials (SYSTEM hive, ntdsutil snapshots); a log-parsing tool (elrs.exe) that harvests logon data from Event ID 4624; lateral movement; a malicious IIS module installed in the GAC that takes commands from cookies and captures submitted credentials; and the Zebracon trojan, which uses compromised Zimbra mail servers and an actor mailbox for command and control [S2]. Unit 42 additionally reports the Godzilla JSP web shell, the Golang NGLite backdoor that uses NKN for C2, and the KdcSponge domain-controller credential stealer [S3][S4]. It also reports SockDetour, a fileless, socketless backup backdoor for Windows servers [S6]. Infrastructure includes commercial VPNs and compromised consumer routers [S1].

campaigns.name: SockDetour backdoor (possible earliest use)
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 assesses from a compilation timestamp that SockDetour may have been in the wild since at least July 2019 [S6].

campaigns.name: SolarWinds Serv-U zero-day (CVE-2021-35211)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft attributes exploitation of a Serv-U SSH zero-day to DEV-0322 with high confidence and reports targeting of US Defense Industrial Base entities and software companies [S1].

campaigns.name: ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus exploitation (CVE-2021-40539)
campaigns.summary: CISA/FBI/CGCYBER warn on 2021-09-16 that APT actors are exploiting the flaw [S7]. Microsoft first observes a DEV-0322 campaign on 2021-09-22 and attributes it with high confidence [S2]. Unit 42 reports at least nine compromised organizations and at least 370 US servers targeted, using Godzilla, NGLite and KdcSponge [S3][S4].

campaigns.name: TiltedTemple ServiceDesk Plus exploitation (CVE-2021-44077)
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 reports that the actor exploited ServiceDesk Plus, with reconnaissance against a US financial organization first seen on 2021-10-25, raising the TiltedTemple total to at least 13 compromised organizations. Unit 42 links part of this activity to Microsoft's DEV-0322 [S5].

campaigns.name: SockDetour against US defense contractors
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 discloses SockDetour, tied to TiltedTemple infrastructure. At least four US defense contractors were targeted and at least one was compromised [S6].

diamond.adversary: China-based operators that Microsoft tracks as DEV-0322 / Circle Typhoon [S1][S2][S8]. No named individuals or sponsoring agency appear in the sources gathered.
diamond.capability: Zero-day and n-day exploits for Serv-U and ManageEngine [S1][S2][S5]. Web shells (Godzilla), a malicious IIS module, NGLite, KdcSponge, the Zebracon trojan and SockDetour [S2][S3][S6]. Credential dumping [S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Commercial VPNs and compromised consumer routers [S1]. Compromised Zimbra servers and an actor-controlled mailbox for C2 [S2]. The NKN peer-to-peer network for NGLite C2 [S3]. A C2 server that hosted SockDetour, a memory-dumping tool and web shells [S6].
diamond.victim: US Defense Industrial Base, software/IT, higher education and consulting organizations [S1][S2]. Energy, healthcare and finance organizations in the TiltedTemple cluster [S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection against the US defense industrial base and technology supply base, consistent with PRC strategic and military-technology interests (inferred from victimology in [S1][S2][S6]; no source states intent beyond espionage access).
diamond.technology: Internet-exposed managed file transfer (Serv-U) and identity and IT-service-management portals (ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus, ServiceDesk Plus) that sit next to Active Directory [S1][S2][S5]. IIS web servers and Zimbra mail servers [S2].

gaps: No public Microsoft profile of activity under the name 'Circle Typhoon' (post-2023 renaming) was found. All Microsoft reporting located uses DEV-0322 and dates to 2021.

Microsoft maps APT27 and Emissary Panda to both Circle Typhoon and Linen Typhoon, and also maps APT6 here [S8]. The source documents do not explain the basis for these mappings. Do not merge APT27/APT6 historical reporting into this record without vendor confirmation.

Unit 42 TiltedTemple and Microsoft DEV-0322 overlap but are not confirmed identical. Unit 42 attributes only part of TiltedTemple to DEV-0322 and could not rule out multiple actors behind SockDetour [S5][S6].
The Unit 42 reports (unit42.paloaltonetworks.com) could not be fetched. Their details come from search excerpts and press coverage, and exact publication dates should be verified.
The CISA advisory AA21-259A could not be opened directly. It names no actor, and its link to DEV-0322 is only by shared CVE [S7].
Specific victims, data stolen, and any activity after 2022 are not public in the sources gathered.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID is recorded for Circle Typhoon/DEV-0322.

Press coverage conflicts on whether the Serv-U exploitation actually hit Defense Industrial Base targets (a later The Hacker News update disputed it), so treat Microsoft's [S1] targeting statement as Microsoft's observation.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): The key cyber terrain is internet-facing enterprise middleware that brokers identity and files: managed file transfer (Serv-U), self-service password and AD portals (ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus), and IT service desks (ServiceDesk Plus) in defense-industrial-base and IT supplier networks [S1][S2][S5]. STEP 2 (effects): Compromising these appliances gives direct paths to domain controllers and credentials [S2][S3]. The actor exploited flaws as zero-days or within days of disclosure, which compresses patch windows [S1][S2][S7]. STEP 3 (threat model): Exploit an edge application, drop a web shell or IIS module, dump credentials (ntdsutil, SYSTEM hive, KdcSponge), move laterally, and keep backup access through stealthy backdoors (NGLite over NKN, SockDetour, Zebracon over compromised Zimbra) [S2][S3][S6]. STEP 4: MLCOA is quiet credential theft and persistent espionage access in DIB contractors and their IT providers through newly disclosed enterprise-software flaws [S2][S6]. MDCOA is harvesting domain credentials at scale across many DIB suppliers at once, enabling follow-on access to programs supporting Air Force missions (inferred from [S2][S3][S6]). Candidate indicators: unexpected child processes of Serv-U.exe or rogue Serv-U global users [S1]; new GAC-registered IIS modules or a key.dat file under ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA [S2]; Godzilla JSP web shells on ManageEngine servers [S3]; ntdsutil snapshot activity [S2]; NKN traffic from servers [S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: Track DIB partners and mission-relevant suppliers that expose Serv-U, ManageEngine or similar identity and IT-service tools, and fuse vendor and CISA vulnerability alerts with exploitation reporting, given zero-day and rapid n-day use [S1][S2][S7]. Authorities: Most victims are private DIB and IT firms [S1][S2][S6], so response depends on DC3/DCISE, CISA and FBI channels and contractor reporting obligations rather than DODIN authorities. Defensive actions inside the DODIN fall to JFHQ-DODIN/AFCYBER service lines. Mission assurance: Domain-credential theft at suppliers can expose program data and shared trust relationships, so assess supplier identity dependencies for mission-critical programs [S2][S3][S6]. Coordination: Share indicators such as IIS module persistence, Zimbra-based C2 and NKN beacons with DIB ISAC partners and CISA, and coordinate with Microsoft and Unit 42 reporting, keeping vendor cluster names (DEV-0322 vs TiltedTemple) distinct [S2][S5][S6].
